summary: The root رَسَسَ (rassasa) primarily means to lay a foundation or to originate something.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.gloss: Love entered, and established itself, in his heart; disease in his body; The fever commenced

parts.t: Love entered, and established itself, in his heart,

headwords.def: رَسَّ الهُوَى فِى قَلْبِهِ , and السُّقْمُ فِى جِسْمِهِ , [aor., accord. to the general rule, رَسِسَ ,] inf. n. رَسٌّ and رَسيسٌ , Love entered, and established itself, in his heart, and disease in his body; as also . (M.) [It seems also, from explanations of رَسُّ and رَسِيسٌ mentioned below, that one says رَسَّتِ الحُمَّى , meaning The fever commenced, or first touched a person. ]

parts.t: when the person attacked thereby stretches on account of it, and becomes languid in his body, and relaxed,
the first that a man feels of the touch of fever, before it takes him forcibly, and becomes apparent.
(As, TA.) Accord. to Fr, you say,
The fever became settled in his bones.

headwords.def: رَسٌّ The beginning, or commencement, of a thing. (K.) And hence, (K,) رَسُّ الحُمَّى , and , The beginning, or commencement, (M, A, K,) or first touch, (S,) of fever, (S, M, A, K,) before it becomes vehement, or severe; (A;) i. e., when the person attacked thereby stretches on account of it, and becomes languid in his body, and relaxed, or heavy, sluggish, or torpid, or confused in his intellect: (M, TA:) or the first that a man feels of the touch of fever, before it takes him forcibly, and becomes apparent. (As, TA.) Accord. to Fr, you say, أَخَذَتْهُ الحُمَّى بِرَسٍّ , meaning, The fever became settled in his bones. (TA.) [Hence also,] رَسُّ الحُبِّ , and , The beginning, or commencement, of love: (K:) or a remain, or relic, or trace, of love:

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
